account: The Water Technology Centre at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI) in New Delhi built a basin-irrigation controller that uses soil-moisture sensors and preset moisture thresholds. The use case states that this threshold controller was tested and deployed at the institute's research farm. It names Monalisha Pramanik, Manoj Khanna and P. S. Brahmanand of the Water Technology Centre as contacts. The team proposes using AI rainfall predictions to control the irrigation gates. A forecast of rain for the next day would close the gate. Otherwise, the motor could open it when soil moisture is low. The team plans pilots across crops and climatic zones. Water savings and other benefits from the proposed AI extension remain unmeasured. A cited water-saving figure comes from separate research on the threshold controller.

ai_role.statement: The sequence diagram explicitly proposes AI rainfall prediction as an input to irrigation-gate decisions. Its effect has not been separately evaluated; existing threshold-based automation is a different component.
